hooks.text: A black hole shoots plasma jets at half light speed.
Did you know the first confirmed black hole shoots dancing jets?
The first black hole ever found is tearing its neighbor apart.

title: The First Confirmed Black Hole's Dancing Jets
description: Discover how Cygnus X-1, the first confirmed black hole, shoots superheated plasma jets at half the speed of light.

beats.text: A black hole shoots plasma jets at half light speed.
beats.visual: Artist concept of Cygnus X-1 binary system and accretion disk, NASA, 2011
queries: Cygnus X-1 black hole artist concept

beats.text: Discovered in nineteen sixty-four, Cygnus X-one is history's first confirmed black hole.
beats.visual: Aerobee sounding rocket launch representing the 1964 discovery, White Sands, 1964

beats.text: It sits seven thousand light-years away in the constellation Cygnus.
beats.visual: Constellation Cygnus night sky map, ESO, 2015

beats.text: The beast pairs with a blue supergiant star named HDE 226868.
beats.visual: Blue supergiant star HDE 226868 field of view, Digitized Sky Survey, 2000

beats.text: They orbit each other every five point six days.
beats.visual: Accretion disk and corona gas heating diagram, NASA, 2012

beats.text: The black hole continuously strips material into an accretion disk.
beats.visual: Black hole accretion disk diagram, NASA, 2018

beats.text: These jets shine with the energy of ten thousand suns.
beats.visual: Relativistic jets shooting from a black hole, NASA, 2019

beats.text: Stellar winds make the plasma jets visibly dance and wobble.
beats.visual: Radio telescope array data visualization for jet observation, NRAO, 2021

beats.text: That explains why a black hole shoots plasma jets at half light speed.
beats.visual: Artist concept of Cygnus X-1 binary system, NASA, 2011
